text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, even for someone who did not write it. One key habit is following naming conventions. This means choosing clear, meaningful names for variables and functions, so their purpose is obvious. Another important idea is keeping functions small and focused. Each function should do one job well. When code is clean, it is much easier to maintain. Developers can find and fix bugs faster, and adding new features becomes simpler. In short, clean code saves time and prevents confusion for everyone on the team.
